Pectoralis Major.name: Pectoralis Major
Pectoralis Major.anatomicalLocation: Anterior upper chest wall (clavicular and sternocostal heads, inserting into the bicipital groove of the humerus)
Pectoralis Major.mainFunction: Helps move the upper arm across the body (horizontal adduction), flexes the shoulder, and internally rotates the humerus during pressing movements.

Deltoids.name: Deltoids (Anterior, Lateral & Posterior)
Deltoids.anatomicalLocation: Caps the glenohumeral shoulder joint across the clavicle, acromion, and spine of the scapula
Deltoids.mainFunction: Abducts, flexes, and extends the humerus to raise and stabilize the arm overhead and laterally.

Biceps Brachii.name: Biceps Brachii
Biceps Brachii.anatomicalLocation: Anterior compartment of the upper arm between the scapula and the radial tuberosity
Biceps Brachii.mainFunction: Flexes the elbow joint and supinates the forearm during curling and pulling movements.

Triceps Brachii.name: Triceps Brachii (Long, Lateral & Medial Heads)
Triceps Brachii.anatomicalLocation: Posterior compartment of the upper arm inserting into the olecranon process of the ulna
Triceps Brachii.mainFunction: Extends the elbow joint and locks out the arm during pressing and pushdown exercises.

Brachioradialis.name: Brachioradialis & Forearm Flexors
Brachioradialis.anatomicalLocation: Lateral and anterior forearm spanning from the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus to the distal radius
Brachioradialis.mainFunction: Generates crushing grip strength, stabilizes the wrist, and assists with elbow flexion.

Rectus Abdominis & Obliques.name: Rectus Abdominis & External Obliques
Rectus Abdominis & Obliques.anatomicalLocation: Anterior and lateral abdominal wall spanning from the costal cartilages to the pubic crest and iliac crest
Rectus Abdominis & Obliques.mainFunction: Creates 360-degree intra-abdominal bracing pressure to protect the lumbar spine and flexes/rotates the trunk.

Trapezius & Rhomboids.name: Trapezius & Rhomboids
Trapezius & Rhomboids.anatomicalLocation: Upper and mid-posterior thoracic back spanning from the occipital bone and spinous processes to the scapula
Trapezius & Rhomboids.mainFunction: Retracts, elevates, and depresses the scapulae to stabilize the upper back under heavy loads.

Latissimus Dorsi.name: Latissimus Dorsi
Latissimus Dorsi.anatomicalLocation: Broad posterolateral back spanning from the thoracolumbar fascia and iliac crest to the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
Latissimus Dorsi.mainFunction: Adducts, extends, and internally rotates the shoulder during vertical and horizontal pulling movements.

Erector Spinae.name: Erector Spinae (Spinal Erectors)
Erector Spinae.anatomicalLocation: Paired paraspinal columns running along the lumbar and thoracic vertebrae
Erector Spinae.mainFunction: Extends the vertebral column and maintains rigid neutral spine alignment against forward shear forces.

Gluteus Maximus & Medius.name: Gluteus Maximus & Medius
Gluteus Maximus & Medius.anatomicalLocation: Posterior pelvis spanning from the ilium and sacrum to the gluteal tuberosity and iliotibial tract
Gluteus Maximus & Medius.mainFunction: Powerfully extends and externally rotates the hip joint while stabilizing pelvic alignment.

Quadriceps.name: Quadriceps Femoris (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Medialis & Intermedius)
Quadriceps.anatomicalLocation: Anterior thigh compartment inserting via the patellar tendon into the tibial tuberosity
Quadriceps.mainFunction: Extends the knee joint and controls eccentric knee flexion during squats, leg presses, and lunges.

Adductors.name: Adductor Magnus & Longus
Adductors.anatomicalLocation: Medial compartment of the thigh spanning from the pubis and ischium to the linea aspera of the femur
Adductors.mainFunction: Adducts the thigh and assists with hip extension out of the bottom of a deep squat.

Hamstrings.name: Hamstrings (Biceps Femoris, Semitendinosus & Semimembranosus)
Hamstrings.anatomicalLocation: Posterior compartment of the thigh spanning from the ischial tuberosity to the proximal tibia and fibula
Hamstrings.mainFunction: Extends the hip during hinge movements and flexes the knee joint.

Gastrocnemius & Soleus.name: Gastrocnemius & Soleus (Calves)
Gastrocnemius & Soleus.anatomicalLocation: Posterior lower leg inserting via the Achilles tendon into the calcaneus (heel bone)
Gastrocnemius & Soleus.mainFunction: Plantarflexes the ankle joint to propel the body upward during calf raises, walking, and jumping.

Tibialis Anterior.name: Tibialis Anterior
Tibialis Anterior.anatomicalLocation: The tibialis anterior is located at the front of the lower leg, lateral to the tibia.
Tibialis Anterior.mainFunction: Helps with dorsiflexion of the ankle and stabilizes the foot and knee during movements like squats, walks, and jumps.
